html:
The Siege of Yorktown was fought from 28 September to 19 October 1781 at Yorktown, Virginia, in today's United States. An American and French army under George Washington and the Comte de Rochambeau trapped a British army under Lord Cornwallis, who surrendered. It was the last major battle of the American Revolutionary War.

After a hard campaign in the southern states, Cornwallis moved his 8,000 men to the port of Yorktown to be supplied by sea. Washington and Rochambeau saw a chance. A French fleet under Admiral de Grasse sailed from the Caribbean and beat off the British fleet at the mouth of Chesapeake Bay on 5 September, closing the sea. The two generals marched about 700 km south from New York with some 17,000 men. They dug trenches ever closer and shelled the town day and night. On 14 October they stormed two key forts, one in an attack led by Alexander Hamilton. Cornwallis asked for terms three days later.

When the news reached London, the government fell within months and Parliament voted to stop the war. In the Treaty of Paris of 1783 Britain accepted the independence of the United States.
